 Order

The petitioner has preferred this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing of impugned order dated 07.02.2018 and for discharge along with quashing of case No.300/2011 along with all subsequent proceedings, pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen, District Raisen (M.P.).
2.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen, District Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner was working as Assistant Manager- Quality Assurance with Parle Agro Pvt. Ltd hereinafter referred to as "the Company".
The said company is incorporated and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 having its registered at "Off Western Express Highway, Sahar- Chakala Road, Parsiwada, Andheri (East), Mumbai 400099".

The aforesaid company is engaged in the business of manufacturing, marketing and distribution of "Ready -To- Serve Juice Based and Synthetic Beverages (Carbonated and Non-Carbonated)" and Packaged Drinking Water, through its various manufacturing plants and sales Offices in India.
The aforesaid company had its manufacturing unit in Raisen, hereinafter referred to as "the Plant".
The petitioner was posted in the said plant at the time of alleged incident and he was the nominee of the company under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

3. On 15.07.2006 the Food Inspector appointed under Section 9 of the Act, inspected the plant and drew a sample of loose chemical flavour (orange coloured) powder, which is used as an ingredient in the manufacturing of Frooti, i.e Ready - To- Serve Fruit Beverage, on the basis of suspicion of being adultered.
The Food Inspector considered the product to be food item/product.
On 17.07.2006 the sample was sent for analysis to the Food Safety Lab, in Bhopal.

4. After a period of more than one month from the date of drawing of sample, the Food Safety Lab,
vide analysis report dated 24.08.2006 found the sample to be misbranded and opined that the misbranded ingredients were used by the Company.
The Food Inspector after a period of almost 5 years from the date of drawing sample sought sanction for prosecution from the Assistant Controller on 04.12.2010.
The Assistant Controller accorded the sanction for prosecution on 14.02.2011.

The prosecution was ultimately launched on 18.04.2011 after the lapse of almost 5 years from the date of drawing of sample for the offences under Sections 7(i), 16(1)(a)(i) and 2(xi) of the Act. and the rules framed there under.
The complaint was registered as case No.300/2011 and is pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On 23.04.2011 the notice was issued and the petitioner appeared before the Court and sought discharge by way of filing application on 09.04.2012 under Section 227 read with Section 245(2) of the Cr.P.C.
It was inter-alia pointed out by the petitioner that the sample of chemical flavour could not have been drawn as the same is not the finished product, which is sold independently in the market.
It was also pointed out that the prosecution of the petitioner is hit by law of limitation as the complaint was filed after a period of about 5 years from the date of drawing of the sample.

With reference to Rule 32(b) of the Rules, the chemical Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/
2 flavour is only a flavouring agent and its contents are not required to be disclosed.

entities.text: Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contents of the aforesaid chemical flavouring has not come forth even in the report of the Chemical Analyst.
The trial Court did not adjudicate the application for discharge and kept the same in abeyance vide order dated 04.10.2012.
Thereafter, the trial Court insisted upon adducing the evidence on 24.08.2016.
Thereafter another application was filed seeking discharge on the same grounds.

The trial Court vide order dated 21.09.2016 dismissed the application on the ground that the cognizance of the offence has already been taken and, therefore, while passing the order dated 21.09.2016, the trial Court did not advert to the grounds raised by the petitioner in the application for discharge.
That is how on the next date of hearing i.e. 22.09.2006, trial Court proceeded to frame charges against the petitioner.
Against the rejection of the application and framing of charges on 28.11.2016, the petitioner preferred a Revision Petition before the Court of Sessions at Raisen.
The Revisional Court vide order dated 14.07.2017 held that the order dated 21.09.2016 was not in accordance with law and the same was not the speaking order.
The order was set- aside and the case was remanded to the trial Court to adjudicate the application dated 09.04.2012 afresh.

On remand the trial Court re-adjudicated the application for discharge and again rejected the same vide order dated 07.11.2017, which according to the petitioner was again a non speaking order and was against the spirit of order of remand.
The trial Court held that the case is an old case and is pending at the stage of consideration of the application for discharge.
The Court has to see only a prima facie material on record.
The order dated 07.11.2018 was again assailed by the petitioner in the revision before the Court of Sessions.

The Revisional Court vide impugned order dated 07.02.2018 dismissed the revision petition on the ground that the sample falls within the defination of food and the same has been found to be misbranded.

The Court while dismissing the revision petition has relied upon the ratio of Adalat Prasad Vs. Rooplal Jindal & Others, AIR 2004 SC 4674 i.e. the trial Court has no jurisdiction to recall/review the order.

entities.text: Adalat Prasad Vs. Rooplal Jindal & Others, AIR 2004 SC 4674
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Revisional Court did not advert to the ground of limitation pointed out by the petitioner.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently submitted that the sample in question was tested after more than 1 month from the date of drawing of sample.
The report of Food Safety Lab indicated that the sample was misbranded.
A note appearing in the report of the Public Analyst showed that the loose sample was found in plastic jar.
The physical appearance of the sample was orange coloured powder without any taste and odour, alleged to be flavour of indicated material by the Food Inspector.
The label was loose sample, having no information about the ingredients inspite of the inquiry made while recording note in the report.

The Public Analyst has only opined that no class of flavour indicated as required under Rule 32(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,
1954.
Only on that count, the sample was found to be misbranded.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the sanction for prosecution was granted on 14.02.2011 and prosecution was launched on 18.04.2011, after a period of more than 5 years from the date of drawing of sample.

In terms of Rule 32(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1954,
labelling of prepackaged foods shall carry the information in the following manner:-
"32(b) Labelling of Prepackaged Foods-

Every package of food shall carry the following information on the label:-

sentences.text: (1) The Name of the Food - The name of the food shall include trade name or description of food contained in the package.
With reference to the aforesaid requirement the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the chemical flavouring itself is not a food item and is not be consumed independently.
No specification/ingredients are specified for preparing this chemical flavour as the same is to be added in the manufacturing process so as to enhance the taste of the product.

The ingredients of chemical flavouring have not been prescribed anywhere in the rules, therefore, violation of the Rule 32(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration, Rules, 1955 is not attracted, as there cannot be any trade name of the chemical flavour, nor has the chemical flavour any description, therefore, the ingredients of the chemical flavour cannot be spelt out by any stretch of imagination.
No reasons have been assigned in the order granting prosecution.
7. The defination of Food even if, includes chemical flavour, the same is to be identified as a finished product for the purposes of analysis.
The Analyst report is silent as to how the sample was found to be misbranded.
The report does not show the shelf life of the sample.
The building of the case on the basis of a flavour against the reality of the sample of a flavour powder, which is chemical in itself cannot be consumed and is not sold by the petitioner.
The universal reality is that every flavour and every chemical flavour has a shelf life and does not usually survive for long period except in a very rare of the rarest case.

The report of the Analyst did not say anything about the chemical properties of the sample and inordinate delay has been caused in testing the sample as well as in granting sanction and launching prosecution thereof.
As per Section 468 Cr.P.C there is a bar to take cognizance after the lapse of the period of limitation.

Section 468 of Cr.P.C is reproduced hereinunder:-
"468. Bar to taking cognizance after lapse of the period of limitation.-

( 1 ) Except as otherwise provided elsewhere in this Code, no Court, shall take cognizance of an offence of the category specified in sub-Section (2), after the expiry Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80431712/
4 of the period of limitation.

entities.text: Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) The period of limitation shall be- (a) six months, if the offence is punishable with fine only;

(b) one year, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year;
(c) three years, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding one year but not exceeding three years.

[(3) For the purposes of this section, the period of limitation, in relation to offences which may be tried together, shall be determined with reference to the offence which is punishable with the more severe punishment or, as the case may be, the most severe punishment.]
8.
In the instant case, the limitation period is maximum 3 years, but the cognizance has been taken after a period of 5 years.
The limitation period commenced on the date of the offence i.e. 15.07.2006 and ultimately ended on 15.07.2009, but the complaint was filed on 18.04.2011.

As per Section 13(2)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 on the receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub Section 1 to the effect that the article of the food is adultered, the Local Health Authority shall, after the institution of the prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14(a), forward in such a manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if, it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.
Evidently, Section 13(2) of the Act is mandatory in nature.
A legal and indefeasible right has been given to the person/accused to get the second sample analysed by the Central Food Laboratory after the receipt of copy of the report.

After the report of the analysis the Local (Health) Authority after institution of the prosecution has not forwarded copy of the report to the petitioner, requiring the petitioner to opt for second analysis/testing by the Central Food Laboratory.
The mandatory requirement of the law in terms of Section 13(2) of the Act has not been complied with and such a non compliance would result in acquittal/discharge of the accused from the charges.

While rejecting the application, the Court has not adverted to the order of granting sanction which is totally non speaking, as no reasons have been assigned as to how and why the sample is misbranded and falls within the ambit of Section 2(ix) of the Act to attract prosecution.

The sanction was sought by the Food Inspector after a period of 5 years from the date of drawing of sample and that fact itself speaks volume about the illegality and arbitrariness of the prosecution case.
9. Moreover the sanction has been granted in a very mechanical manner without application of any judicial mind.
On second occasion, the discharged application was dismissed without application of mind, solely on the ground that the review is not permissible in view of Adalat Prasad (supra) case.
The Court has not appreciated the fact that there is a difference between the order of summoning and order for framing charge.
The discharge can only be sought at the stage of framing of charge(s).

entities.text: Nand Kishore Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It cannot be held that the review is applicable as the order of summoning has been passed.

The order of summoning is a distinct stage and order of framing charge is a second stage and summoning of the accused cannot be used to say that the application for discharge is hit by the concept of review.

10. Keeping in view the entirety of the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that the prosecution has miserably failed to bring home the necessary ingredients of the offence against the petitioner.
No material exist for charging the petitioner with the offence.

The prosecution case is hit by limitation, mandatory non compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, delay in obtaining sanction and the order granting sanction being a mechanical order.

In view of the aforesaid non-compliance of the mandatory provisions of law, I deem it appropriate to quash the impugned order dated 07.02.2018 and all subsequent proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof.

Normal consequence to follow since no offence is made out against the petitioner, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, therefore, Case No.300/2011 pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen (M.P.) is ordered to be quahsed along with all subsequent proceedings.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
11. For the reasons recorded hereinabove, this Petition is allowed.
